newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti revises down gain from PC sale.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti revises down gain from PC sale.

text.p: Italian high-tech group Olivetti said it had revised down the financial benefit gained from the sale of its personal computer division to Piedmont International earlier this year to 190 billion lire from 250 billion.

Olivetti said in a statement the estimate had been updated at the request of Italian stock market regulator Consob and the downward revision was due to a lower valuation of the PC business's net assets.

The revision also took into account of a "temporary" extension of Olivetti's holding in Piedmont, currently 19.7 percent against a stake of some 12 percent initially held after the sale was carried out last April.

Olivetti stock closed 5.02 percent down at 641 lire in Milan on Friday, the day after it announced that its consolidated revenues for the first half of 1997 stood at 3.1 trillion lire, down 10.4 percent on the same 1996 period.
